page: OVHcloud d2-4 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Discovery family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model and no hyperthreading. Memory capacity is limited to 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address with a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics falling into the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, measuring 19.19 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 14.22 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these hardware limitations, with a Passmark CPU score of 2054.9 and a database operations score of 980.18. Despite these constraints, the server achieves 2.07 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.89 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest hardware profile, the d2-4 offers a highly cost-efficient option for non-production environments where resource density and low overhead are prioritized over raw compute power. The lack of dedicated CPU threads and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 limits its utility for intensive processing. This server is best suited for lightweight, budget-conscious workloads such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, small Redis caching nodes, or low-traffic utility applications.
